#### What this PR does / why we need it:


The pod worker may recieve a new pod which is marked as terminal in
the runtime cache. This can occur if a pod is marked as terminal and the
kubelet is restarted.

The kubelet needs to drive these pods through the termination state
machine. If upon restart, the kubelet receives a pod which is terminal
based on runtime cache, it indicates that pod finished
`SyncTerminatingPod`, but it did not complete `SyncTerminatedPod`. The
pod worker needs ensure that `SyncTerminatedPod` will run on these pods.
To accomplish this, set `finished=False`, on the pod sync status, to
drive the pod through the rest of the state machine.

This will ensure that status manager and other kubelet subcomponents
(e.g. volume manager), will be aware of this pod and properly cleanup
all of the resources of the pod after the kubelet is restarted.

While making change, also update the comments to provide a bit more
background around why the kubelet needs to read the runtime pod cache
for newly synced terminal pods.

This change fixes issue #116925. Also introduce a new regression test for
#116925 which restarts the kubelet while a pod is terminating and
ensures the pod is properly deleted. This test currently fails on master
without this change.

It looks like to me the issue here is that the kubelet is being restarted in a bit of an unfortunate time resulting in at least two related issues:

### Issue 1

The pod status has been updated on the api-server to terminal `Succeeded` just prior to the kubelet restarting.  The status manager did not yet complete [deleting the pod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e7eca7fd38454200819b60e58144d5727f1bbc/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L856-L870).

Then after kubelet restarts and comes back up, it attempts to add this pod `SyncLoop ADD`, (even though it is in terminal phase). This seems like the first issue: if the pod phase is terminal on the API server, we probably should not add it back.

### Issue 2

The pod worker receives the `SyncPodCreate`, but the pod worker quickly terminates (`Pod is finished processing, no further updates`). I am assuming this is because of [this check](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L777-L792), i.e. based on pod cache lookup the pod is terminal. 

The side affect of this is that the status manager never receives the signal that the pod is `finished` (which is normally done as part of `SyncTerminatingPod`. This is because in this case, we never call `kl.generateAPIPodStatus(pod, podStatus, true)` which sets `finished` to be true. As a result, I think [`canBeDeleted` check](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e7eca7fd38454200819b60e58144d5727f1bbc/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L887-L902) will never return true, so this pod will never be able to be deleted.

I have made a test which will reproduce this behavior in a node e2e, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117019.

It can be reproduced by starting a pod and then deleting it and triggering kubelet restart at the right time. A watch is setup to trigger a kubelet restart as soon as the pod enters the succeeded phase. If the kubelet restart happens before the kubelet is able to delete the pod on the API server, but after the phase is updated, then we trigger the issue. The pod will be re-added to kubelet after restart, but will never be deleted on the API server despite it having a deletion timestamp set and being in terminal phase.

I tried the same test on 1.26 and it passes. This is because on 1.26, the status manager phase to terminal happens at roughly at the same time when we delete the pod. 

On 1.27+, after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115331, the status phase to terminal can happen earlier and the status manager can skip deleting the pod because `isFinished` [is false](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e7eca7fd38454200819b60e58144d5727f1bbc/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L896-L901). In this case, after start, `isFinished` will never be true, so the pod never will get deleted.

But in general pods can be in terminal phase and not be deleted (like plain pods and pods from jobs). They would eventually be deleted by the pod GC otherwise.

Is this a bug in the device plugin?

> But in general pods can be in terminal phase and not be deleted (like plain pods and pods from jobs). They would eventually be deleted by the pod GC otherwise.

That is true, but the issue here is that the pods have a deletion timestamp set as well. If the deletion timestamp is set and the kubelet is up, it is the kubelet's responsibility to terminate and delete those pods. 

> Is this a bug in the device plugin?

This doesn't have anything with device plugin, rather we caught the issue due to the device plugin test which asserts that all pods are terminated and deleted prior to starting the test.

> If the deletion timestamp is set and the kubelet is up, it is the kubelet's responsibility to terminate and delete those pods.
